extracted.intended_audience: NRC licensees, nuclear facility operators, counsel, and members of the public interested in NRC license amendment, comment, and hearing procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register monthly notice from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission listing proposed and issued amendments to facility operating/combined licenses, proposed No Significant Hazards Consideration (NSHC) determinations, and procedural instructions for submitting comments, requests for hearing, and electronic filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Significant Hazards Consideration (NSHC) criteria (10 CFR 50.92)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Commission's regulations in 10 CFR 50.92, operation of the facilities in accordance with the proposed amendments would not (1) involve a significant increase in the probability or consequences of an accident previously evaluated; or (2) create the possibility of a new or different kind of accident from any accident previously evaluated; or (3) involve a significant reduction in a margin of safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the facility-specific amendment requests shown in this notice, the Commission finds that the licensees' analyses provided, consistent with section 50.91, are sufficient to support the proposed determinations that these amendment requests involve NSHC. The Commission will consider public comments in making any final determinations and may issue amendments before the normal waiting period if the final determination is that the amendment involves NSHC or if circumstances (e.g., imminent derating or shutdown) require timely action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee analysis consistency with 10 CFR 50.91
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees' analyses provided, consistent with section 50.91 of title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) 'Notice for public comment; State consultation,' are sufficient to support the proposed determinations that these amendment requests involve NSHC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ADAMS accession number for each document referenced (if available in ADAMS) is provided the first time it is mentioned. Applicants and others should refer to the application (and ADAMS accession numbers) for the detailed analyses supporting the NSHC determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period and treatment of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any comments received within 30 days after the date of publication of this notice will be considered in making any final determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must be filed by the stated comments close date (document-specific; e.g., October 2, 2025 for this notice). The NRC encourages electronic comment submission through Regulations.gov and will post all comment submissions on Regulations.gov and enter them into ADAMS. The NRC does not routinely edit comment submissions to remove identifying or contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to request a hearing and petition to intervene (10 CFR part 2, 2.309)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after the date of publication of this notice, any person whose interest may be affected may file a request for a hearing and petition for leave to intervene with respect to that action. Petitions shall be filed in accordance with the Commission's Agency Rules of Practice and Procedure in 10 CFR part 2 (see 10 CFR 2.309).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition is filed the Commission or a presiding officer will rule on the petition and, if appropriate, a notice of a hearing will be issued. Petitions and motions for leave to file new or amended contentions that are filed after the deadline will not be entertained absent a determination by the presiding officer that the filing demonstrates good cause by satisfying the three factors in 10 CFR 2.309(c)(1)(i)–(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Late filings / good cause standard (10 CFR 2.309(c)(1)(i)-(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions and motions for leave to file new or amended contentions that are filed after the deadline will not be entertained, absent a determination by the presiding officer that the filing demonstrates good cause by satisfying the three factors in 10 CFR 2.309(c)(1)(i) through (iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice directs interested persons to consult a current copy of 10 CFR 2.309 for the detailed three-factor test and supporting requirements for demonstrating good cause for late filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: State/local/Tribal participation (10 CFR 2.309(h) and 2.315(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A State, local governmental body, Federally recognized Indian Tribe, or designated agency thereof may submit a petition to participate as a party under 10 CFR 2.309(h) no later than 60 days from the date of publication. Alternatively, such entities may participate as a non-party under 10 CFR 2.315(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For information about filing a petition and about participation by a person not a party under 2.315, the notice cites ADAMS accession and NRC resources (including the NRC adjudicatory participation webpage) for procedural guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submissions / E-Filing requirements (10 CFR 2.302)
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents filed in NRC adjudicatory proceedings must be filed in accordance with 10 CFR 2.302. The E-Filing process requires participants to submit and serve adjudicatory documents over the internet (or in some cases mail copies on electronic storage media) unless an exemption permitting an alternative filing method is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To comply: at least 10 days prior to the filing deadline, contact the Office of the Secretary to request a digital ID certificate and advise the Secretary that you will be submitting a petition or other adjudicatory document; after obtaining a digital ID and docket creation, submit adjudicatory documents in PDF; a filing is considered complete at the time it is submitted through the E-Filing system; timely electronic files must be submitted no later than 11:59 p.m. ET on the due date; the system timestamps submissions and sends confirmation emails and distributes access to Office of General Counsel and others who have advised the Secretary they wish to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-Filing assistance, help desk, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A person filing electronically may seek assistance by contacting the NRC's Electronic Filing Help Desk via the NRC site-help pages, email, or toll-free call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help Desk is available between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m., ET, Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays. The notice lists specific contact points and URLs for e-submission guidance and getting started with digital ID certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions to electronic filing (10 CFR 2.302(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants who believe they have good cause for not submitting documents electronically must file an exemption request in accordance with 10 CFR 2.302(g) with their initial paper filing stating why there is good cause and requesting authorization to continue to submit in paper format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such filings must conform to 10 CFR 2.302(b)-(d). Participants granted an exemption under 2.302(g)(2) must still meet the electronic formatting requirement in 2.302(g)(1) unless they also seek and are granted an exemption from that formatting requirement. Participants filing in paper are responsible for serving their documents on all other participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and copyrighted material guidance for filings/comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC cautions commenters not to include identifying or contact information they do not want publicly disclosed; participants are requested not to include personal privacy information (e.g., SSNs, home addresses, personal phone numbers) in filings unless required by regulation or law. With respect to copyrighted works, except for limited excerpts that serve the purpose of the adjudicatory filings and would constitute a Fair Use application, participants should not include copyrighted materials in their submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NRC will post comment submissions and enter them into ADAMS and does not routinely edit to remove identifying/contact information. If aggregating comments from others, requesters should inform those persons not to include identifying/contact information they do not want publicly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to documents and referencing guidance (ADAMS and PDR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly available information related to this action may be obtained via Regulations.gov (Docket ID), NRC ADAMS Public Documents collection, and the NRC's Public Document Room (PDR). When contacting the NRC about availability of information, refer to Docket ID, facility name, unit number(s), docket number(s), application date, and subject; ADAMS accession numbers for each document referenced (if available in ADAMS) are provided the first time they are mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADAMS web search instructions and PDR appointment/contact information are provided, and users are directed to the ADAMS accession numbers included in the notice for locating application materials and safety evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical exclusion / NEPA applicability (10 CFR 51.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise indicated, the Commission has determined that these amendments satisfy the criteria for categorical exclusion in accordance with 10 CFR 51.22 and thus, pursuant to 10 CFR 51.22(b), no environmental impact statement or environmental assessment need be prepared for these amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commission has prepared an environmental assessment under the special circumstances provision in 10 CFR 51.22(b) and made a determination based on that assessment, it is indicated in the safety evaluation for the amendment. The safety evaluation provides ADAMS accession numbers for the application and the Federal Register citation for any environmental assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official publication and legal notice guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays an XML rendition of the Federal Register as an unofficial prototype; the PDF linked (govinfo.gov) is the official electronic format. The XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts until the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register issues a regulation granting it official legal status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those relying on FederalRegister.gov for legal research should verify results against an official edition (PDF on govinfo.gov). For public inspection, the FR Doc PDF is identified and users are warned to verify contents against a final, official edition.
